Fix by setting the WinHTTP system proxy and a **WU bypass list**, or making the proxy\\\\n  allow unauthenticated access to the WU URLs.\\\\n- **TLS 1.2 not enabled** (handshake fails on modern endpoints): enable TLS 1.2 + `SchUseStrongCrypto`.\\\\n- **Outdated/missing root certs** (`0x800B0109`/`0x800B010A` untrusted chain): refresh the root store\\\\n  (`certutil -generateSSTFromWU` + `-addstore Root`), enable root auto-update.\\\\n- **Clock skew** (`0x80072F8F`): a wrong clock makes valid certs look invalid \\\\u2014 fix time first.\\\\n- **Firewall / WPAD**: outbound 443 (or 8530/8531 for WSUS) blocked, or WPAD pointing at a bad proxy.\\\\n\\\\n## Diagnosis first\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the connectivity fault before acting (read-only):\\\\n  ```powershell\\\\n  $wu=\\'HKLM:\\\\\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\\\\\Policies\\\\\\\\Microsoft\\\\\\\\Windows\\\\\\\\WindowsUpdate\\'\\\\n  (Get-ItemProperty \\\\\"$wu\\\\\\\\AU\\\\\" -Name UseWUServer -EA SilentlyContinue).UseWUServer\\\\n  (Get-ItemProperty $wu -Name WUServer -EA SilentlyContinue).WUServer\\\\n  netsh winhttp show proxy\\\\n  Get-Date; do not keep retrying). Otherwise it\\'s a Microsoft-Update path issue (proxy/TLS/cert).\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: **Fix the transport** for Microsoft-Update: WinHTTP proxy + WU bypass (SYSTEM context), enable TLS 1.2, refresh the root cert store \\\\u2014 as applicable.\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: **Verify** a `Microsoft.Update.Session` search / HTTPS to a WU endpoint succeeds.\\\\n\\\\n## Validation (check your own work before reporting success)\\\\n- [ ] The source was correctly identified (WSUS vs Microsoft Update) \\\\u2014 a WSUS-unreachable case was escalated, not force-retried.\\\\n- [ ] If proxy: the WU bypass is set in the **SYSTEM/WinHTTP** context (not just per-user IE), and the WU endpoints are reachable.\\\\n- [ ] A `CreateUpdateSearcher().Search(...)` (or HTTPS GET to a WU endpoint) succeeds with no 407/timeout/cert error.\\\\n- [ ] The originally failing scan no longer fails on connectivity.\\\\nIf any check fails, re-classify \\\\u2014 don\\'t disable cert validation or loop-retry against an unreachable WSUS.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n- **`UseWUServer=1` + unreachable WSUS is an infrastructure problem, not an OS fix** \\\\u2014 escalate to the WSUS/network owner; repeatedly re-running the patch fails identically and wastes the window. A `UseWUServer=0` fallback is temporary (GPO reverts it) and needs approval.\\\\n- **SSM patches as SYSTEM** \\\\u2014 a proxy that works for interactive users can 407 for SYSTEM because it has no cached credentials; set the WinHTTP proxy + a WU bypass list, or make the proxy allow the WU URLs unauthenticated.\\\\n- **`0x80072F8F` is often a wrong clock, not a cert problem** \\\\u2014 check `Get-Date`/NTP before touching the cert store.\\\\n- **Cert errors split two ways** \\\\u2014 `0x80072F8F` (clock/TLS) vs `0x800B0109`/`0x800B010A` (untrusted root chain); the latter needs a root-store refresh, not a clock fix.\\\\n- **WU bypass must be in the WinHTTP (system) proxy**, not only WinINET/IE per-user \\\\u2014 the WUA uses WinHTTP.\\\\n- **Don\\'t disable TLS certificate validation to \\\\\"fix\\\\\" it** \\\\u2014 enable TLS 1.2 and trust the correct roots instead.\\\\n\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"SKILL.md\", \"automation/iam-policy.json\", \"reference/wsus-routing.md\", \"reference/root-certs-and-clock.md\", \"reference/tls-settings.md\", \"reference/proxy-system-context.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "20e939bf-7a41-4177-8d3c-0e4069e9ec80", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's the root cause and the fix.

## Why it fails only under SSM

**AWS-RunPatchBaseline runs as SYSTEM (LocalSystem), not as your logged-in admin user.** That's the entire story:

- Windows Update Agent uses the **WinHTTP (system-wide) proxy configuration**, not the per-user Internet Options/IE proxy settings.
- When you're logged in interactively, your proxy settings often come from your user profile or a WPAD/PAC file resolved in your user context — and if the proxy needs NTLM/Kerberos auth, your cached domain credentials authenticate silently.
- SYSTEM has **no cached proxy credentials** and generally can't complete NTLM/Kerberos auth to a proxy. So when the patch scan tries to reach Microsoft Update endpoints through the proxy, the proxy returns **407 Proxy Authentication Required**, which Windows Update Agent surfaces as `0x80244017` (`WU_E_PT_HTTP_STATUS_DENIED`).

In short: same machine, same proxy, different identity — and only one of those identities can authenticate.

## The fix

**1. Diagnose (read-only, confirms the mismatch):**
```powershell
netsh winhttp show proxy
Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings' | Select ProxyEnable,ProxyServer
Test-NetConnection windowsupdate.microsoft.com -Port 443 -WarningAction SilentlyContinue
```
If `netsh winhttp show proxy` shows "Direct access (no proxy server)" while your logged-in user has a proxy configured, that confirms SYSTEM has no proxy path at all — or if it does have one set, SYSTEM still can't auth to it.

**2. Set the WinHTTP (system) proxy with a Windows Update bypass list** — this is the actual fix, since WUA reads WinHTTP, not WinINET/IE:
```powershell
$cur = netsh winhttp show proxy 2>&1
if($cur -match 'Proxy Server'){
  $proxy = ($cur | Select-String 'Proxy Server').ToString() -replace '.*:\s+',''
  $bypass = '*.windowsupdate.microsoft.com;*.update.microsoft.com;*.download.windowsupdate.com;*.download.microsoft.com;169.254.169.254;169.254.169.123'
  netsh winhttp set proxy proxy-server="$proxy" bypass-list="$bypass" | Out-Null
} else {
  netsh winhttp import proxy source=ie | Out-Null
}
Restart-Service wuauserv -Force
```

**3. Verify:**
```powershell
netsh winhttp show proxy | Select-String windowsupdate
try{ (Invoke-WebRequest https://windowsupdate.microsoft.com -UseBasicParsing -TimeoutSec 15).StatusCode; "PROXY OK" }catch{ "still $($_.Exception.Response.StatusCode.value__)" }
```

## Important caveat

If your corporate proxy enforces **NTLM/Kerberos authentication**, setting the WinHTTP proxy alone won't fully solve it — SYSTEM still can't do interactive-style auth to the proxy. In that case you have two real options:
- Get the proxy admins to allow the Windows Update / Microsoft Update URLs **unauthenticated** (the bypass list above only works if those destinations don't require the proxy at all, or the proxy whitelists them).
- Route WSUS/Microsoft Update traffic through an internal path that doesn't require proxy auth (e.g., VPC endpoint/PrivateLink where applicable, or an internal WSUS reachable without the corporate proxy).

Rollback if needed: `netsh winhttp reset proxy`.

Want me to pull up the instance in SSM and check its current WinHTTP proxy state and connectivity to confirm this is indeed what's happening before you apply the fix?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
